quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Before you change lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.
Look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, you must check behind you. Look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Also check that no other drivers are trying to move into the same spot.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped ahead to pick up or drop off children, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop until all children have left the bus.
Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops with red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, you must stop completely. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back before you go. Even after the bus moves, do not proceed until you are sure no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase the chance of a crash.
Improves your ability to react to dangers.
Often leads to unsafe decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to unsafe decisions.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to unsafe decisions.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Brake hard.
Do not drive through the flood. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only through the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the flood. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through a flooded road. Shallow-looking water can hide dangers. If you find a flooded area, turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:

options.text: The vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
The yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means that traffic on that side can pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: To turn quickly, your hands must be:

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
At the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position helps you turn safely and comfortably on roads with higher speeds.

questions.question: There are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right. You should steer:

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
Down the middle between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right, steer down the middle between them.

questions.question: A driving distraction is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. Distracted driving can cause crashes that damage property, injure people, or cause death.

questions.question: If weather or lighting requires you to use your headlights:

options.text: Use your parking lights.
Use your high beams.
Use your low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beam light reflects back and causes glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to ensure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently with increasing pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly when traffic is heavy or weather is bad. However, if you drive so slowly that you block normal traffic flow, you can be cited.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from:

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start the turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you be a better driver.
Make you feel better.
Hurt your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hurt your judgment.
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, being tired slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and hurts your judgment.

questions.question: Bicycles on the road:

options.text: Must always yield to motor vehicles.
Do not follow specific rules of the road.
Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles on the road are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Motor vehicle drivers should respect bicyclists' rights.

questions.question: You can drive off the road to pass another vehicle:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes in your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, use your turn signals:

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
When approaching the curb, but not when leaving it.
When approaching or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When approaching or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signals when approaching a curb to park and when leaving the curb.

questions.question: This sign warns you are approaching:

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. This sign is placed a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Use only the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.
Use only the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Look several times if needed. Watch traffic in front of you and next to you.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Judge the distance to oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judge the distance to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. They may seem slower than they really are. Only pass when you are sure you can safely change lanes. If you are unsure of an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes and you have enough space to safely change lanes.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all corners, yield to:

options.text: Any driver on your left.
Any driver who arrived before you.
Any driver across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any driver who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: After stopping completely, vehicles go through a four-way stop in the order they arrived. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: Bad suspension can cause:

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Slack in the steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and keeps your ride smooth over bumpy roads. If your car bounces a lot after hitting a bump or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Ease up on the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the ignition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease up on the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal to regain control. Steer in the direction of the skid to help the vehicle recover.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is a major cause of crashes. Any distraction causes drivers to miss important signs and sounds needed to avoid accidents.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Stop.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming.

questions.question: Check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Do not stare at one spot while driving. Check your rearview mirrors often so you know where vehicles near you are located.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means that vehicles:

options.text: Driving in both directions may pass.
Next to the broken line may pass.
Next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop.
At a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely at a red traffic light. You must always obey a police officer directing traffic, even if signs or signals say otherwise.

questions.question: At a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Wait for the green light before proceeding.
Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
Stop before crossing the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be alert. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians, then proceed with caution.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while in a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic on the road (within posted speed limits). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes often happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.
